name: Retrieval Tester
blurb: which chunks of your documents a query retrieves, ranked by BM25, with the matching words shown
intro: Indexes pasted chunks with Okapi BM25 (k1 and b adjustable, optional stemming and stopwords) and shows, for each query, which chunks come back in what order, how much each query word contributed, and - when expected chunk ids are given - recall@k and MRR. Lexical only: embeddings are not computed.

inputs.label: Documents / chunks
inputs.help: Markdown (each #, ## or ### heading starts a chunk; id = the heading slug or an explicit {#id}), plain paragraphs, or JSONL / a JSON array with id and text (as Chunking Planner writes).

inputs.label: Queries
inputs.default:
how do I flash new firmware over USB => dfu-update
update rolled back to the previous version => ota-ab, boot-loop
device keeps restarting every few seconds => boot-loop, tr-guncelleme
RST_CAUSE IWDG after reboot => watchdog
what baud rate is the console => uart-console
battery lasts how many years => power, tr-pil
cihaz sürekli yeniden başlıyor => tr-guncelleme, boot-loop
connect to an enterprise wifi network => wifi-provisioning
terminating resistor value => can-termination
inputs.help: One per line. Optional expected chunk ids after =>, comma separated. # starts a comment.

inputs.label: k1 (term frequency saturation)
inputs.help: 0 = only presence counts; 1.2-2.0 is usual (Lucene default 1.2).

inputs.label: b (length normalisation)
inputs.help: 0 = chunk length ignored, 1 = fully normalised (Lucene default 0.75).

examples.title: API docs as JSONL chunks, no stemming, k1 = 1.5

input.queries:
why do I get 401 invalid_token => api-auth-02
too many requests error => api-rate-01
how to get the next page of devices => api-pag-01
verify webhook signature => api-web-01
what should I send support => api-err-01

usage: Give docs (Markdown with headings, paragraphs, or JSONL/JSON with id and text), queries (one per line, optional `=> expected-id, ...`), k1, b, stem (none, en, tr, en+tr), stopwords and topk. Returns per query the top-k chunk ids with BM25 scores, the first rank of an expected chunk, recall@k and MRR over the queries, warnings for queries that match nothing and odd chunk sizes, and the rankings as JSONL. Use it to check a RAG corpus's chunking and query wording before adding embeddings, or to see why a chunk is not found.
sources: S. Robertson, H. Zaragoza, 'The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond', Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval 3(4), 2009 (eq. 3.15)
Apache Lucene BM25Similarity documentation (IDF = ln(1 + (N - n + 0.5)/(n + 0.5)), defaults k1 = 1.2, b = 0.75)
Manning, Raghavan, Schutze, 'Introduction to Information Retrieval' (2008) ch. 8.4 (MRR) and 8.3 (recall)
Cormack, Clarke, Buettcher, 'Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual rank learning methods', SIGIR 2009 (hybrid note)
Stemmers and stopword lists: light suffix strippers written for this tool, not Porter/Snowball
